# Travel Preferences

I feel calmer on trips when the first day has no scheduled activity after hotel check-in. Morning flights are preferable to overnight flights, and an aisle seat matters more than a meal upgrade. For rail journeys, I like a quiet carriage and a table seat when one is available. A useful itinerary should keep transfers longer than twenty minutes and should show one backup connection instead of packing the day with optional stops.

## Food Boundaries

I enjoy small neighborhood restaurants and tasting menus, but I avoid shellfish because of an allergy. Very spicy food is uncomfortable, while vegetarian dishes and mild regional specialties are welcome. When suggesting dinner, I would rather walk fifteen minutes than take a taxi across town. Reservations after 8:30 PM are usually too late, especially on a work night.

# Work Rhythm

Deep work is easiest for me before lunch, particularly between 8:30 and 11:30 in the morning. I prefer to batch administrative messages after lunch and leave Friday afternoons free for review and planning. Meetings without an agenda are draining, and a thirty-minute default is better than an hour. If a deadline is flexible, I would rather deliver a polished draft the next morning than rush an incomplete version late at night.

## Learning Style

I retain technical material best when an explanation starts with a concrete example, names the underlying rule, and ends with a small exercise. Long videos are hard to revisit, so written notes with commands and expected output are more useful. When I am stuck, a hint that narrows the search space is preferable to a complete solution. I like spaced review after one day, one week, and one month.
